title: The closing instructions changed
scenario: The day before a home purchase closes, an email that looks like it came from the title company says its receiving bank changed after a “security upgrade.” It includes new wire instructions and warns that late funds could delay the keys.

answers.A: Use the new instructions because the email has the correct property address, closing amount and staff signature.
answers.B: Call the title company or closing attorney using a number from earlier paperwork—not the email—and verbally verify the account details before sending anything.
answers.C: Pause the transfer and ask for the bank change to be confirmed through the established closing portal or in person.

explanation: Real-estate wire fraud often relies on compromised email and accurate transaction details. A changed payment destination deserves independent verbal verification.
proTip: For large wires, verify the destination using a contact method established before the change.
